rows.ARS:
Orange or orange-red Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: Catalònia (pernetiana, Dot 1931)
rows.Origin:
Bred by Pedro (Pere) Dot (Spain, 1931).
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 1933 as 'Catalònia'.
Introduced in France by Henri Guillot in 1934 as 'Catalònia'.
Introduced in Australia by Hazlewood Bros. Pty. Ltd. in 1935 as 'Catalònia'.
rows.Bloom: Crimson or cardinal red, golden-yellow shading. Moderate fragrance. Medium to large, very double, borne mostly solitary, in small clusters, flat, globular bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Bushy, well-branched. Glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 4' to 5' (120 to 150cm). Width: up to 4' (up to 120cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b through 10b. Vigorous. Disease susceptibility: susceptible to blackspot . Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
rows.Parentage:
seed:

rows.Notes: Arena Rose Co.'s Catalog 2000 says Catalonia is an older Hybrid Tea by the Spanish hybridizer, Pedro Dot. It produces large blooms of salmon-apricot on long, straight stems...

colour: Crimson or cardinal red, golden-yellow shading.
